note: A beginner guitar week at 20 minutes a day: a short hands warm-up, chord changes, A minor pentatonic box 1 returning in five new forms (slow, roots, faster, in E, from memory), and every day ending on something musical.

plan.title: Week 1: box 1 and clean changes
plan.summary: A minor pentatonic box 1 from first notes to improvising, with G-C-D and power chord changes in time and a tune a day.

days.theme: Box 1 meets G, C and D

exercises.title: The spider
exercises.focus: Fingers 1234 from the 1st fret, every string, 60 bpm

sections.text: One finger per fret wakes up all four fingers before you need them.

Fingers 1 2 3 4 on frets 1 to 4 of the low E, then the same on each string up to the high E, and back down. One note per click; keep each finger down until the next string. Done when no note buzzes for a whole climb.

exercises.title: G, C and D in time
exercises.focus: G-C-D-G changes · down strums at 60 bpm

sections.text: G, C and D are the I, IV and V of G major, so these three changes unlock hundreds of songs.
The shapes
Fret each shape, strum once and pick each string to check it rings. Then switch G to C, C to D, D to G, slowly, five times each.
In time
Press Play and strum down on every beat, one bar per chord. Done when you land every change on beat 1 for two passes.

exercises.title: Box 1 at 60
exercises.focus: A minor pentatonic · box 1 · 60 bpm, then the roots

sections.text: Box 1 is home base for lead guitar: every note sits under your fingers at the 5th fret.
Up and down
Play the box from the low {{1}} to the high E string and back, one note per click, alternate picking.
Only the roots
Play only the three {{1}} notes (A) in the box, low to high and back, saying "A" each time.

exercises.title: First phrases
exercises.focus: Box 1 over drums in A · end on A

sections.text: Improvising with a few notes is how the box becomes music and not a pattern.
Over the band, play phrases of three notes from box 1 with a gap after each. End every phrase on a {{1}}.

exercises.title: Spider, new order
exercises.focus: Fingers 1324 from the 3rd fret, 60 bpm

sections.text: Changing the finger order makes each finger move on its own, not just follow the one before.
Fingers 1 3 2 4 starting at the 3rd fret, every string up and back. Slow enough that every note rings.

exercises.title: A5, D5, E5
exercises.focus: Power chords A5-D5-E5 · eighth notes at 70 bpm

sections.text: A power chord is only a root and a 5th, so one shape moves anywhere and works in any rock riff.
One shape, three places
Index on the root, ring finger two frets up on the next string. Mute the other strings with the side of your index. Move between the three shapes ten times.
In time
Press Play and strum each chord twice per beat, down-down, one bar each. Done at two passes with no ringing open strings.

exercises.title: Box 1: roots and 5ths
exercises.focus: A minor pentatonic · box 1 · 1 and 5 lit

sections.text: The two notes of a power chord are also in box 1; finding them links your riffs to your solos.
Play box 1 up and down once at 70. Then play only {{1}} and {{5}} (A and E), low to high and back, and hear the power chord's sound in single notes.

exercises.title: A five-note tune
exercises.focus: Sol Fa Mi Re Do in C, from tab

sections.text: Short tunes from tab train your hands to find notes you hear in your head.
A tune walking down from Sol to Do. Press Play to hear it, then play along from the tab. Done at three clean passes.

exercises.title: Box 1 at 70, then 80
exercises.focus: A minor pentatonic · box 1 · 70 → 80 bpm

sections.text: Speed comes from small steps up in tempo once a slower one is clean.
At 70
Box 1 up and down, starting on the low {{1}}, twice clean in a row.
At 80, from the middle
Now at 80, starting on the {{1}} on the D string: up to the top, down to the bottom, back up to where you started.

exercises.title: One-minute changes: G and C
exercises.focus: G-C changes · best count in one minute

sections.text: G to C is the change that trips most beginners; counting it shows you it getting faster.
Change G to C and back as many times as you can in one minute, one strum per chord. Three rounds; write down your best clean count.

exercises.title: Do Mi Sol tune
exercises.focus: Do Mi Sol Mi Do in C on the neck

sections.text: A tune on the home chord's notes shows you where a melody sits around the C chord.
Press Play and play along in the neck view, then in tab. The tune uses only {{1}} {{3}} {{5}} (C, E, G).

exercises.title: Call and response in box 1
exercises.focus: Two-bar phrases in A · box 1 · 80 bpm

sections.text: Answering your own phrase is the simplest way to make a solo sound like it is going somewhere.
Play a two-bar phrase, rest two bars, then play an answer that starts like the first and ends on a {{1}}. Keep going for the whole time.

exercises.title: The spider, higher up
exercises.focus: Fingers 1234 from the 5th fret, 70 bpm

sections.text: At the 5th fret the frets are closer, so you can push the tempo a little.
Fingers 1 2 3 4 from the 5th fret, every string up and back at 70. Keep your thumb behind the neck.

exercises.title: G-Em-C-D strumming
exercises.focus: Down, down-up, up-down-up · G-Em-C-D at 70 bpm

sections.text: One strum pattern held steady over changes is what makes chords sound like a song.
The pattern on one chord
On G only, strum down, down-up, up-down-up, counting "1, 2 and, and 4 and". Keep your hand moving down and up even when it misses the strings.
Over the changes
Same pattern, one bar per chord, with the band. Done at two passes without stopping.

exercises.title: Sol La Sol
exercises.focus: A tune with La in G, from tab

sections.text: La, one step above Sol, is the note that gives many folk tunes their lift.
Press Play to hear it, then play along from the tab: Sol La Sol Mi Do. Then once in the neck view.

exercises.title: Box 1 phrases over A
exercises.focus: Box 1 · phrases ending on C, then on A

sections.text: Changing the note a phrase ends on changes how finished it sounds.
Over the band, end four phrases on {{b3}} (C): they sound open. Then end four on {{1}} (A): they sound closed. Alternate the two.

exercises.title: Spider, 1324
exercises.focus: Fingers 1324 from the 1st fret, 70 bpm

sections.text: Low on the neck the stretch is widest, so this is where the spider builds reach.
Fingers 1 3 2 4 from the 1st fret, every string up and back at 70.

exercises.title: E5, G5, A5 riff
exercises.focus: Power chords E5-G5-A5 · 80 bpm

sections.text: These three are the power chords of E minor, so they fit today's scale.
Press Play and strum each chord down on every beat, one bar each, muting with your palm near the bridge. Done at two clean passes.

exercises.title: E minor pentatonic, two places
exercises.focus: E minor pentatonic · open position, then box 1 at the 12th fret

sections.text: Box 1 is a shape, not a place: move it and you have the scale in any key.
Open position
E minor pentatonic with open strings: play it from the low {{1}} (open E) up and back at 70. Every open string is in the scale.
The same notes at the 12th fret
The shape you know from A, moved to the 12th fret: it is the open position again, an octave higher. Up and back at 70, starting on the {{1}}.

exercises.title: Improvise in E
exercises.focus: Open E minor pentatonic over drums

sections.text: Open strings ring under fretted notes, which is why E is a favourite key for guitar solos.
Over the band, mix fretted notes with open strings; end each phrase on the open low {{1}}.

exercises.title: The spider at 80
exercises.focus: Fingers 1234 from the 3rd fret, 80 bpm

sections.text: A small tempo step up shows the week's progress in your fingers.
Fingers 1 2 3 4 from the 3rd fret, every string up and back at 80. Drop to 70 if notes start to buzz.

exercises.title: G, C, D: the count
exercises.focus: G-C and C-D one-minute changes

sections.text: Counting again shows how far the changes have come since day 3.
One minute of G to C, then one minute of C to D, one strum per chord. Two rounds each; compare with your day 3 count.

exercises.title: Box 1 without the chart
exercises.focus: A minor pentatonic · box 1 from memory at 80

sections.text: Playing a shape without looking is the test that it is really yours.
Play box 1 up and down at 80 without looking at the chart. Then check against it and fix any wrong note. Last, play only the {{1}} notes from memory.

exercises.title: A longer tune
exercises.focus: A Sol-stage tune in G, tab then neck

sections.text: A longer tune asks you to remember phrases, not single notes.
Learn it from tab
Press Play to hear it, then play along from the tab one phrase at a time.
Play it through
Now the whole tune in the neck view at 75. Done at two passes without stopping.

exercises.title: G-Em-C-D, full pattern
exercises.focus: Strum pattern over G-Em-C-D at 80 bpm

sections.text: The week's chords at a faster tempo, to hear how far they have come.
Down, down-up, up-down-up, one bar per chord, at 80. Done at four passes without a stop.

exercises.title: Box 1 in A and E
exercises.focus: Minor pentatonic box 1 · A, then E at the 12th fret

sections.text: Playing one shape in two keys back to back proves you know the shape, not the frets.
Box 1 in A at 80, up and down, starting on the {{1}}.
Now the same shape at the 12th fret, in E, starting on its {{1}}.

exercises.title: Jam over Am and G
exercises.focus: A minor pentatonic box 1 over Am-G

sections.text: Two chords and one box is a real jam, the kind you can play with friends.
Land on the roots
Press Play and improvise in box 1. Land on {{a}} when Am comes round and on {{g}} when G does.
Free
Same backing; now play whatever you like from the box, using the call and response from day 3.

exercises.title: Your tune, for the record
exercises.focus: Day 6's tune in G at 75 bpm

sections.text: Recording a tune you learned this week gives you something to compare next week against.
Play day 6's tune twice along with the app, then record one take on your phone.
